title: Unified assured-PNT operational awareness and decision support (single pane for source health, composite confidence, jam/spoof triage, fallback recommendation) with a formation-level PNT interference picture feeding the C2/EW COP
version_designed_for: NARROWER VERSION ONLY (verdict was BORDERLINE, G04-score.json). This diligence designs the vendor-neutral composite-assurance ENGINE: an ASPN 2023 / pntOS-C-conformant plug-in that ingests 3-8 heterogeneous PNT sources at 1-10 Hz and emits per-source health, composite confidence with attributed evidence, explainable fault/jam/spoof classification and a fallback recommendation, plus a synthetic scenario generator and a replay/audit library validated against public recordings (TEXBAT, Jammertest 2025) and DHS Resilient PNT Conformance Framework v2.0 behaviors. It explicitly does NOT design the single-pane HMI as the product (a thin demo window only) and does NOT design the formation-level PNT interference picture / EW COP feed (killed: classified-adjacent, NGC2-absorbable). Every plan stage and milestone below is built to test the decisive doubt from the score file: does a named buyer with a budget line or vehicle exist for this engine (NP004 Phase I awardees ~Q1 2027, the GPNTS integrator, the next NAVWAR open-topic/D2P2 cycle, an OT/CSO sponsor, or a paying civil/allied maritime pilot)? All kill criteria are measurable. Nothing here is a legal judgment on ITAR/EAR/FOCI/SBIR eligibility or immigration; those items are flagged for counsel.

architecture.prose: INPUTS. The engine consumes time-stamped PNT observables from three classes of source. (a) A synthetic scenario generator that emits ASPN 2023 schema-conformant messages (GNSS PVT and raw measurements, IMU, clock/timing, an 'alternate source' such as a simulated eLoran/radar-fix/celestial-fix channel) for a strait-transit vignette with scripted jamming onset, spoofing pull-off, INS drift, clock holdover and hardware faults. (b) Public real-world recordings: TEXBAT RF spoofing captures (UT Austin Radionavigation Lab, 25 Msps, 400 s scenarios) replayed through the GPL-3 GNSS-SDR software receiver to produce observables, and the Jammertest 2025 HDF5 interference dataset on Zenodo (CW, PRN, chirp, multi-emitter, spoofing, meaconing, with time-aligned ground truth). (c) Commercial receiver and IMU telemetry from bench hardware: u-blox ZED-F9P boards (UBX-MON-RF jamInd, AGC, per-satellite C/N0, NMEA/UBX), a MEMS IMU (Xsens MTi-3 class), and a bench timing reference for clock-holdover modelling; RF recordings are injected by CONDUCTED cable into a shielded enclosure only, never radiated. In a government phase the same ingest layer takes GPNTS ICD adapters and pntOS fusion-engine outputs (government-furnished post-award; FACT that ICDs are post-award, G04.json). COMPUTE is commodity: an x86 laptop or NUC-class box running an OCI container (Docker/Podman) fully disconnected; target footprint under one CPU core and 2 GB RAM at 10 Hz so it can co-host on a shipboard CANES-class server later (HYPOTHESIS on hosting; the Navy has not published GPNTS hosting specs). CORE SOFTWARE has seven modules: K1 ingest/normalisation (ASPN 2023 YAML-generated codecs, a pntOS-C plugin shim, NMEA-0183/UBX adapters); K2 per-source health monitors (ICD-compliance checks, C/N0-AGC anomaly tests, clock-drift/holdover model, RAIM-style residual tests, INS-GNSS divergence, position/velocity jump tests) modelled on the BSD-3 DHS PNT Integrity Library's check structure; K3 the composite confidence and consensus engine, which builds a cross-source consistency graph, weights sources by their health, and outputs a calibrated composite confidence with an attributed-evidence list (which checks fired, on which source, at what time); K4 an explainable classifier that separates hardware fault, jamming, spoofing and environmental degradation using a rule/likelihood hybrid whose every output carries a human-readable rationale; K5 a fallback recommender that maps the classified state and the health of alternates to a recommended mode (alternate source, INS-only, degraded-ops workflow) keyed to the DHS CF Respond/Recover behaviours and to the operator's own TTP table (the TTP table is customer-configurable, not embedded doctrine); K6 an append-only audit/replay store; K7 a scenario/evaluation harness that batch-runs the scenario library and computes the metrics. INTERFACES: ASPN integrity/status messages out through the pntOS plugin API; a language-neutral streaming API (gRPC/WebSocket) for any HMI or fusion engine; a replay file format (HDF5/Parquet); and a deferred, compact interference-report message shape that could later feed a COP (out of scope for this version). OUTPUTS are the six artefacts the Navy's NP004 text asks for in substance: per-source health, composite confidence with evidence, classification with rationale, fallback recommendation with rationale, an auditable timeline, and an evaluation report on held-out scenarios. USERS of the engine are, first, integrators (NP004 Phase I awardees, the GPNTS integrator, allied fusion-engine houses) who embed it behind their own HMI; second, test and evaluation staff who need the replay/audit library; and only third, via the customer's HMI, the ETV/navigation team. A thin ECDIS-style demo window exists solely to make the engine's outputs legible in an operator study.

architecture.hardest_problem: Producing a composite confidence that is CALIBRATED and a classification that is CORRECT across heterogeneous sources whose failure modes overlap (a smooth spoofing pull-off, an INS bias ramp and a receiver clock fault can all look like slow divergence), while keeping every decision explainable and while the real military threat signatures remain classified (GAO-21-320SP: 'determination of assurance is an active research area', FACT/HIGH). The engineering answer is a consensus-plus-physics architecture: per-source physical plausibility checks (C/N0-AGC signatures, clock-drift bounds, IMU-propagated position bounds) to separate jamming from spoofing from faults, cross-source residual voting to bound composite confidence, and a rule/likelihood hybrid rather than an opaque model so rationale is always available. The residual risk is domain shift: an engine tuned on TEXBAT/Jammertest and synthetic data will meet unseen signatures in a Navy data set; the mitigation is to design for post-award retraining/retuning with a documented calibration procedure rather than claiming generality (INFERENCE/MEDIUM).

architecture.integration_burden: MVP: low-to-moderate and entirely under the founders' control (open schemas, COTS serial telemetry, file-based replay). Military prototype: HIGH and outside the founders' control - the government owns every decisive interface (GPNTS ICDs post-award, ASPN stewardship reportedly moving to the ISTO consortium in 2026 (MEDIUM), RAISE/OSA accreditation, CANES hosting via PMW 160), and the GPNTS integrator controls day-to-day access; each Navy/Army/allied customer needs its own ICD-conformance adapter, which is the 'consultancy trap' the score file warns about. The architecture limits the burden by keeping all customer-specific code in the K1 adapter layer and by making the pntOS plugin API the only contract the core engine depends on. Expected effort per new military integration: 3-9 engineer-months plus government test time (HYPOTHESIS/LOW).

performance_metrics.metric: Detection latency from anomaly onset to first health/confidence change
performance_metrics.why: NP004 specifies 1-10 Hz ingest and the Navy's success metric is 'speed to decision during an anomaly' (FACT, G04.json); sub-second engine latency keeps the human, not the software, as the bottleneck

performance_metrics.metric: Classification accuracy (hardware fault vs jamming vs spoofing vs environmental) on held-out synthetic + public real recordings
performance_metrics.target: >= 90% correct on held-out synthetic; report per-class confusion on TEXBAT ds1-ds8 and Jammertest 2025 scenarios with no cherry-picking
performance_metrics.why: The Navy's metric is 'threat comprehension accuracy'; TEXBAT and Jammertest provide ground truth so the number is auditable (targets are HYPOTHESIS - no published Navy threshold)

performance_metrics.target: < 1 alert per 24 h of clean transit data (clean static/dynamic TEXBAT, clean Jammertest segments, own bench logs)
performance_metrics.why: Watchstanders ignore noisy tools; DHS CF v2.0 notes 'untrustworthy does not always mean the current solution is incorrect' (FACT), so alarms must be evidence-attributed and rare

performance_metrics.target: Reliability diagram / Brier score reported; confidence within +/-10% of empirical correctness per bin on held-out scenarios
performance_metrics.why: An uncalibrated 'confidence gauge' is the dashboard failure mode the score file says will be absorbed; calibration is the engine's differentiator

performance_metrics.metric: Correct-fallback selection and time-to-fallback in an operator study
performance_metrics.target: >= 30% faster median time to correct fallback and fewer wrong selections vs a fragmented-display baseline, n >= 6 former ETV/QM/navigators, pre-registered protocol
performance_metrics.why: NP004 Q&A 2026-08-26 names 'decision accuracy (e.g., correct fallback selection)' as a success metric (FACT); this is the evidence integrators and the GPNTS office can cite

performance_metrics.target: 100% of outputs carry an evidence list; bit-identical re-run of any logged scenario
performance_metrics.why: NP004 asks for 'explainable rationale and auditable trace'; after-action review and accreditation reviewers need determinism

performance_metrics.target: 100% schema-valid ASPN 2023 messages in and out; loads as a pntOS-C plugin without modification of the host
performance_metrics.why: The Navy allowed synthetic ASPN/pntOS data in Phase I and any Phase II swaps in GPNTS ICDs; conformance is the price of admission for integrators

performance_metrics.metric: Continuity of output under a compromised source
performance_metrics.target: Output continues, with degraded confidence flagged, while a source is excluded and re-admitted automatically (DHS CF Level 2/3 behaviour)
performance_metrics.why: DHS CF v2.0 defines Respond/Recover behaviours by level (FACT); civil/allied buyers can test against it

performance_metrics.target: < 1 CPU core, < 2 GB RAM, < 200 MB container image, zero network egress
performance_metrics.why: Air-gapped container deployment is an explicit NP004 requirement; co-hosting on existing shipboard servers avoids a hardware line (HYPOTHESIS on host specs)

mvp.demo: A 60-minute, fully offline demonstration on a commercial laptop: (1) the scenario harness plays a synthetic ASPN-2023 strait-transit vignette (8 sources: two GNSS receivers, INS, clock, radar-fix channel, celestial/DR channel, an alternate RF-PNT channel, a timing source) with scripted jamming onset, a slow spoofing pull-off, an INS bias ramp and a receiver hardware fault; the engine, loaded as a pntOS-C plugin, streams per-source health, composite confidence with an evidence list, an explainable classification and a fallback recommendation in under one second per event, into a thin ECDIS-style window; (2) the same engine, unchanged, ingests observables derived from TEXBAT ds3/ds7 and a Jammertest 2025 CW/chirp/spoofing segment and produces the evaluation report (latency, confusion matrix, false-alert rate, calibration); (3) a live bench segment: two u-blox ZED-F9P boards and an MTi-3 IMU inside a shielded enclosure receive a CONDUCTED gps-sdr-sim/bladeRF stimulus that shifts the fix, and the engine flags the receiver-level divergence against the IMU and the second receiver; (4) replay of any moment in the session, bit-identical, with the audit trail; (5) a summary of the operator study (n >= 6 former ETV/QM/navigators) comparing time-to-correct-fallback with and without the engine's outputs. The HMI is deliberately plain; the pitch to integrators is 'drop this plugin behind your screen'.
must_prove: Buyer test (the decisive doubt): at least one named integrator or sponsor with money agrees in writing to evaluate the plugin - an NP004 Phase I awardee (announced ~Q1 2027), the GPNTS integrator, an IWRP/NavalX/DIU sponsor, or a civil/allied maritime operator - otherwise the venture thesis fails regardless of the technology
Composite confidence and classification are correct and calibrated on held-out synthetic AND public real recordings, with a quantified false-alert rate and sub-second latency at 1-10 Hz
Former watchstanders reach the correct fallback faster and with fewer errors when the engine's outputs are present than with fragmented displays (pre-registered protocol, n >= 6)
Every recommendation is explainable and every session is replayable bit-for-bit
The engine consumes a pntOS/ASPN stream unchanged, so a government phase can swap synthetic streams for GPNTS ICD adapters without touching the core
The container runs fully disconnected on commodity hardware within the resource targets and is structured to pass Iron Bank/RAISE-style hardening later (SBOM, no network egress, non-root)

build_plan.work: Customer-discovery sprint runs in parallel with engineering for the whole plan. Engineering: generate ASPN 2023 codecs from the YAML model; stand up the pntOS-C plugin skeleton (Meson wrap); define the internal event model and the replay format; download TEXBAT and Jammertest 2025; build the GNSS-SDR pipeline that converts TEXBAT RF to observables. Business: retain counsel for the eligibility/CUI memo; contact NAVWAR Small Business Office, NavalX, Open-PNT/ISTO community; list likely NP004 bidders and civil/allied maritime operators.

Implement per-source health monitors (K2) on the PNT-Integrity check structure: C/N0-AGC anomaly, clock-drift/holdover, RAIM residuals, position/velocity jump, INS-GNSS divergence. Build the synthetic scenario generator with 10 strait-transit vignettes and ground truth. Order and bench the COTS stack in the shielded enclosure. Recruit the fractional PNT-integrity engineer and the former-watchstander advisor.

Implement composite confidence/consensus (K3) and the explainable classifier (K4) with attributed evidence; first evaluation report on held-out synthetic and TEXBAT/Jammertest data; iterate on calibration. Run the fallback-policy workshop with the watchstander advisor to produce the configurable TTP schema and a sample table (customer-owned content).

Implement fallback recommender (K5), audit/replay (K6) and the streaming API; build the thin ECDIS-style demo window; conducted-RF bench demo with gps-sdr-sim/bladeRF into the receivers. Freeze the pre-registered operator-study protocol; recruit 6-8 former ETV/QM/navigators. Show a private build to 2-3 candidate integrators for feedback (kill-criterion checkpoint 1).

Run the operator study; harden the container (non-root, SBOM, zero egress, size/footprint targets); regression suite over the full scenario library; write the evaluation report. Present at a NavalX/Tech Bridge or ION-type venue; pursue an evaluation agreement/LOI with an integrator or a civil/allied operator.

Buffer and decision month: publish the reference-plugin package (conformance tests, sample streams) to the Open-PNT community as credibility; finalise go/no-go against the kill criteria; if go, prepare the next-cycle NAVWAR open-topic / D2P2 / OT proposal or the subcontract SOW with an awardee.

kill_criteria: By month 4: fewer than 3 substantive technical conversations with likely NP004 bidders, the GPNTS integrator, or allied/civil fusion-engine houses, or none expresses intent to evaluate the plugin -> stop (no buyer signal)
By month 6: no written evaluation agreement, teaming LOI, CRADA path, or paid civil/allied pilot term sheet -> stop or pivot; do not continue on 'interest'

By month 6: the fractional PNT-integrity engineer and the former Navy watchstander are not engaged (paid) -> stop; without them the product is a dashboard (score file: reject if not recruited within six months)

Technical: held-out classification accuracy < 80% or false-alert rate > 4 per 24 h on clean data after month 5 tuning -> the engine is not differentiated; stop or reduce to a services offer without venture framing
Operator study shows no measurable improvement (time-to-correct-fallback not better than baseline at n >= 6) -> the awareness thesis fails for this design

Counsel memo concludes no compliant structure exists for SBIR AND no OT/CSO sponsor is found by month 9 AND no civil/allied paying pilot -> stop (eligibility plus single-customer dependence, the score file's killer risk)

Within 18 months: no funded Navy Phase II/OT (or subcontract on one) with GPNTS ICDs in hand, no scheduled PNTAX/fleet demonstration, and no paying civil/allied pilot -> stop (score file's stated stop rule)

capital_map.does_250k_reach_next_fundable_milestone: YES for Stages 0 and 1 (combined $85k-$190k, typically ~$130k), which is the next FUNDABLE milestone for this borderline opportunity: a validated, standards-conformant assurance engine with an auditable evaluation report and operator-study evidence, PLUS the result of the buyer test (a written evaluation agreement/LOI from an NP004 awardee, the GPNTS integrator, an OT/CSO sponsor, or a paying civil/allied operator). $250k leaves $60k-$165k of runway to keep two founders alive for 3-6 more months while converting that LOI into a funded agreement. $250k does NOT reach Stage 2 (credible field demonstration, $250k-$600k) on its own and does not approach Stage 3 ($0.8M-$2.5M); those require a seed round, an SBIR/OT award, or a subcontract. Important honesty: the milestone that justifies $2-5M of outside capital (score file) is Stage 3's funded Navy Phase II/OT or subcontract with GPNTS ICDs in hand plus one paying civil/allied pilot and a counsel-cleared cap table - $250k buys the evidence needed to get there, not the milestone itself. If Stage 1 ends without a buyer signal, the honest outcome is a services/licensing business or a shutdown, not a venture.
capital_map.next_milestone: Stage 1 complete: pntOS-C-conformant composite-assurance plugin with held-out evaluation report, replay library and operator-study results, hardened offline container, and at least one written evaluation agreement/LOI from a named integrator or sponsor (buyer test passed) - targeted within 6-8 months of start
capital_map.assumptions: Software-only company; founders U.S.-based; all Stage 0-1 work on public/synthetic unclassified data with no CUI; hardware prices from distributor listings found this session (u-blox C099-F9P-1 ~$328; bladeRF 2.0 micro xA4 ~$480; HackRF-class ~$450; Xsens MTi-3 Click ~GBP 527) and otherwise estimates flagged as such; labor rates assumed ($150/h fractional PNT engineer; $140k-$220k FTE for senior engineers); Stage 2-4 ranges are order-of-magnitude judgments (HYPOTHESIS) consistent with S11 capital_intensity ($0.3M-$2M credible military demo; $2M-$8M first production) and are not quotes; government test costs (PNTAX, fleet demo) are assumed largely government-borne; CMMC Phase 2 C3PAO transition is suspended as of July 2026 (E07-F9), so Level 2 self-assessment is assumed through Stage 3; nothing here is a legal judgment on SBIR eligibility, ITAR/EAR, FOCI or immigration.

engineering_risks.risk: Overlapping failure signatures (slow spoof pull-off vs INS bias ramp vs clock fault) make the classifier ambiguous and the composite confidence miscalibrated.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design K2 as physics-based per-source tests (C/N0-AGC, clock bounds, IMU-propagated position bounds) and K3 as cross-source consensus; report calibration curves in the demo on held-out TEXBAT/Jammertest and synthetic data; the demo's evaluation report makes the ambiguity measurable instead of hidden.

engineering_risks.risk: Domain shift: public and synthetic data do not contain real military threat signatures (classified per GAO), so field performance is unknown.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Ship a documented retune/recalibration procedure and a replay harness so a government team can re-validate on its own data post-award; keep rule/likelihood structure inspectable; the demo shows the harness working on two unrelated data sets (TEXBAT vs Jammertest) as a proxy for shift.

engineering_risks.risk: Standards drift: ASPN stewardship reportedly moving to the ISTO consortium (2026, MEDIUM); pntOS-C is a young repo (10 commits at fetch); the government message set is gated.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Generate codecs from the YAML model so schema updates are mechanical; isolate all schema-facing code in K1; participate in the Open-PNT community; the demo proves 'unchanged engine, swapped stream'.

engineering_risks.risk: GPL contamination from GNSS-SDR or OpenCPN into the proprietary engine.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Run GPL tools as separate processes with file/stream boundaries; license audit in Stage 1 legal line; the container image documents its SBOM.

engineering_risks.risk: RF legality: any radiated GNSS-band test signal is illegal; a bench mistake could end the company.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Conducted-only injection inside a shielded enclosure with attenuators and dummy loads; written lab procedure; real over-the-air exposure only in authority-controlled arenas (Jammertest-type) or aboard a partner operator in advisory-listed regions, recording only.

engineering_risks.risk: Operator study is underpowered or biased (small n, founders facilitating).
engineering_risks.mitigation: Pre-register the protocol with the watchstander advisor, counterbalance scenario order, n >= 6, report effect sizes and confidence intervals; treat a null result as a kill signal, not something to explain away.

engineering_risks.risk: The thin demo HMI becomes the product by accident, recreating the absorbable 'dashboard'.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Keep the HMI in a separate repo with a public API contract; sell and demo the plugin to integrators first; the demo's third segment (bench receivers, no HMI, API output only) proves the engine stands alone.

engineering_risks.risk: Integration burden per customer turns the company into a consultancy (score file's warning).
engineering_risks.mitigation: Adapter-only customer code in K1; price adapters as NRE and the core as a license; the Stage 1 conformance test suite lets integrators self-integrate.

engineering_risks.risk: Eligibility/CUI: the non-U.S.-person co-founder cannot touch government data or the gated ASPN message set; SBIR ownership/control test unresolved.
engineering_risks.mitigation: Stage 0 counsel memo; architecture keeps all government-data handling in a separable CUI enclave and role; OT/CSO and civil/allied paths pursued in parallel so the buyer test does not depend on SBIR alone (not a legal judgment).

engineering_risks.risk: Resource footprint or air-gap requirements fail on the eventual shipboard host (specs unknown).
engineering_risks.mitigation: Design to conservative targets (< 1 core, < 2 GB, zero egress) and measure them in the demo; ask integrators for host constraints in Stage 0 interviews.
